claims.text: High-temperature solution treatment can produce a single-phase, homogenized HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
HfNbTaTiZr contains nanoscale compositional and structural fluctuations.
Nanoscale compositional fluctuations produce spatial variations in thermal expansion.
Differential thermal expansion among local regions generates internal stress fields during heating.
Thermal-expansion-induced internal stresses enhance dislocation motion.
Thermal-expansion-induced internal stresses promote short-range ordering.
Enhanced dislocation motion and short-range ordering together explain transitions in creep, hardening, and elastic-modulus behavior.
Rapid quenching minimizes compositional heterogeneity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Slow cooling permits nanoscale compositional fluctuations to develop in HfNbTaTiZr.
Slow-cooled material will have greater local variation in thermal expansion coefficients than rapidly quenched material.
Thermal-expansion mismatch activates additional dislocation glide at elevated temperatures.
Thermal-expansion mismatch activates additional diffusion processes at elevated temperatures.
Internal mismatch stresses stabilize short-range ordering.
Slow-cooled samples will have a higher effective elastic modulus than rapidly quenched samples above 600 °C and up to 1250 °C.
Slow-cooled samples will have better creep resistance than rapidly quenched samples above 600 °C and up to 1250 °C.
Rapidly quenched samples will have lower internal thermal stresses and behavior dominated by intrinsic lattice properties.
The proposed internal-stress effects will be most apparent between 600 °C and 1250 °C and minimal below 600 °C.
Above 1250 °C, phase transformations may confound the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says mismatch stresses enhance dislocation glide and diffusion, processes that can facilitate high-temperature deformation, while the predicted outcome attributes improved creep resistance to those same stresses. The hypothesis does not explain how short-range ordering outweighs the deformation-enhancing processes.
